solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A Dean Koontz book cover with a characteristic style

parts.note: to cover something is to hide it
taken as written
one's way is one's characteristic manner of doing things

explanation.surface: A description of the jacket design on one of Dean Koontz's thrillers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book cover' reads as a dust jacket, but the book is the definition and 'cover' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideaway is the title of a 1992 horror novel by the American writer Dean Koontz.

clue.text: What upset an island queen?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for 'What' is read bottom to top

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
the Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A question about what has upset the queen of some island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is HE + CUBA. 'Island queen' looks like one phrase, but the island belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba was the wife of King Priam and queen of Troy in Greek legend.

clue.text: A brother primarily in an old play

definitions.text: A brother primarily in an old play

parts.words: A brother primarily in an old play
parts.note: surface reading: a sibling who chiefly appears in some old drama

parts.words: A brother primarily in an old play
parts.note: setter's reading: a character who is principally just the brother of the hero, in a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, Duncan's younger son does little except flee to Ireland; he is mainly there as Malcolm's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Donalbain is King Duncan's younger son in Macbeth, a minor role defined largely by being Malcolm's sibling.

clue.text: A musical old lady turning lovey dovey

indicators.note: turning round sends the combined musical and old lady back the other way

parts.note: the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Perón
an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who loves musicals is becoming soppy and sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: EVITA + MA, read backwards, gives AMATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amative means inclined to love or amorous, which is what a lovey-dovey person is.

clue.text: An ideal notion of mornings: hosting 10's partner and bible classes

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the mornings hold the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: two lots of AM, the abbreviation for morning
10 across is Ernie Wise, whose comedy partner was Eric Morecambe
taken as written
RE is religious education, school lessons that include the Bible

explanation.surface: An idealised view of mornings that involve entertaining a comedian and attending Bible study.
explanation.walkthrough: AM and AM go either side of ERIC + AND + RE. Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: The American dream is the ideal of prosperity and success available to all through hard work.

clue.text: A god's love returned by a goddess

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an Egyptian deity of the underworld
second meaning: the husband whom his goddess wife brought back to life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' and 'returned' look like O and a reversal signal, but the second half is a description: the slain god was restored by his wife Isis.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris, Egyptian god of the dead, was murdered by Set and revived by his wife and sister Isis.

clue.text: Jolly Corner's owner, a writer, parks up outside

indicators.note: outside says the parks go around the writer
in a down clue, up means the word for parks is read from the bottom

parts.note: recs are recreation grounds, public parks
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: The owner of a cheerful street corner is a writer surrounded by parks.
explanation.walkthrough: Recs, short for recreation grounds, is British for public parks. 'The Jolly Corner' is a ghost story by Henry James.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Brydon is the protagonist of Henry James's 'The Jolly Corner', returning to his New York house of that name.

clue.text: "Ring of bright water" writer sounds wet

indicators.note: sounds says we want a word heard, not seen

parts.note: rainy weather is wet weather

explanation.surface: A writer about a ring of shining water would naturally sound watery.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavin Maxwell took the title of his otter memoir from a poem by Kathleen Raine.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Kathleen Raine wrote the poem containing the phrase 'ring of bright water', later Maxwell's book title.

clue.text: A course to finish training a climber

parts.note: the sweet, or dessert, is the course that ends a meal
PE is physical education, school physical training
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer completes a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a scented flowering plant that grows upward by clinging with tendrils.

clue.text: Adam was the first reported poet

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we want what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: Adam committed the first sin, so he was the first sinner

explanation.surface: Adam was the earliest poet, as some report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First poet' seems to belong together, but 'the first' completes a description of a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinna the Poet is the character in Julius Caesar torn apart by a mob who mistake him for the conspirator.

clue.text: Half a turn made by an eagle that's like Browning's thrush

indicators.note: the eagle makes up the outside, with the 'an' set within it

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle
an means one, written as the Roman numeral I
Browning's poem 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad' calls it 'the wise thrush'

explanation.surface: A bird of prey turns halfway, acting like the thrush in Browning's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: ERN(I)E + WISE. A turn is a music-hall or variety act; Ernie Wise was one half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise formed one half of the double act with Eric Morecambe, so he was half a comic act.

clue.text: Why a ham can't get the sack in this Shakespeare love story

parts.words: Why a ham can't get the sack
parts.note: surface reading: why a poor actor keeps his job

parts.words: Why a ham can't get the sack
parts.note: setter's reading: a ham is a cured pig with no place to sleep, the sack being bed
a comic 1941 novel about Shakespeare's romance, by Caryl Brahms and S. J. Simon

explanation.surface: An overacting player cannot be dismissed from the cast of a Shakespearean romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham means both a bad actor and cured pork; 'the sack' is both dismissal and slang for bed. Francis Bacon also features in the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a comic novel of Shakespeare's courtship, also featuring Francis Bacon in search of lodgings.

clue.text: "Sebastian and his friend are more interested in — than heiresses" (Lord Marchmain)

definitions.text: "Sebastian and his friend are more interested in — than heiresses" (Lord Marchmain)

parts.words: "Sebastian and his friend are more interested in — than heiresses"
parts.note: surface reading: a quotation with a gap to fill
setter's reading: the speaker is in Brideshead Revisited, and the gap is a Venetian painter

explanation.walkthrough: In Evelyn Waugh's Brideshead Revisited, Lord Marchmain says this in Venice of Sebastian and Charles, who prefer art to marriage prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian Renaissance painter, the kind of artist the young men visit in Venice.

clue.text: He made Murphy signal the end of the race

parts.note: a beck is a gesture of summons, as in at one's beck and call

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of the
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Someone forced a man called Murphy to wave a flag at the finish of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett wrote Murphy, his first published novel, in 1938.

clue.text: Misconstrue an ode and perplex a poet

indicators.note: to misconstrue is to read wrongly, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two parts of the fodder

explanation.surface: Misreading an ode will baffle the poet who wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was the eighteenth-century English poet of The Rape of the Lock and An Essay on Man.

clue.text: One's boss is upset about one producing a thriller by Lionel White

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the one
upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An employee's manager is annoyed about one member of staff writing a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ONESBOSS goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsession is a 1962 crime novel by the American writer Lionel White.

clue.text: Mother superiors have saints, not bishops as judges

indicators.note: have, paired with not, says the mother superiors take one thing in place of another

parts.note: an abbess is the head of a convent
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; these two are swapped out

explanation.surface: Heads of convents take holy men rather than senior clergy as their judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Assesses is a verb meaning evaluates or appraises, which is what one judges.

clue.text: A novel description of the lead character from fans of The Beach?

parts.note: surface reading: the hero is both a devoted son and a lover
setter's reading: people who like the beach love sun and sand, and the title sounds that way

explanation.walkthrough: The Beach is also a novel, by Alex Garland, which makes 'fans' look like readers.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence's 1913 novel follows Paul Morel, torn between his mother and the women he loves.

clue.text: A schedule set up without sex for a chap like Biggles

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first part wraps around sex
in a down clue, set up means raised, so the schedule is read bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
sex is Latin for six, the Roman numeral VI
taken as written

explanation.surface: A timetable is arranged with no sexual content for a boyish adventure hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here keeps its old sense of outside, and 'sex' is Latin, not English. Biggles is the fighter pilot hero of W. E. Johns's boys' books.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggles is a fictional fighter pilot, so a chap like him is an airman.

clue.text: Antigone's end goal is controversial

indicators.note: end asks for the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: the last letter of Antigone
a goal is an aim, a motive for acting

explanation.surface: Antigone's final aim in the Greek tragedy is a matter of dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feelings, so it is likely to be disputed and contentious.

clue.text: This compiler's half French: the one who moans a lot

definitions.text: the one who moans a lot

indicators.note: half says to keep only the first four of the eight letters

parts.note: this compiler is Myrtilus, the setter of the puzzle
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being half French and a habitual complainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The French for 'the' is LE, so 'French' together with the colon's 'the' supplies it. Moaning Myrtle is the ghost in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: Moaning Myrtle haunts a girls' bathroom at Hogwarts, forever wailing and complaining.

clue.text: His spider helped a friend with bee trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters get stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's pet spider came to the aid of a friend who had a problem with a bee.
explanation.walkthrough: In Charlotte's Web, the spider Charlotte saves her friend Wilbur the pig by weaving words into her web.
explanation.definitionFit: E. B. White wrote Charlotte's Web, whose spider rescues her friend from slaughter.

clue.text: A composer who gave us a music lesson

definitions.text: A composer who gave us a music lesson

parts.words: A composer who gave us a music lesson
parts.note: surface reading: a musician who once taught us

parts.words: A composer who gave us a music lesson
parts.note: setter's reading: a German Romantic opera composer who also wrote critical essays on music

explanation.walkthrough: Several famous composers share the surname, from Carl Maria von Weber to Andrew Lloyd Webber with an extra B.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was a German Romantic composer of operas such as Der Freischütz.

clue.text: This Nobel Laureate could be expansive without using a media company

indicators.note: without using says one letter is left out of the word for expansive

parts.note: broad means wide, expansive
the letter A, removed
Sky is the British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A prizewinner might be expansive if he avoided a particular media firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Brodsky, the Russian-American poet, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1987.

clue.text: Incredibly small boat with music playiing

indicators.note: playing about with the letters lets them fall into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny boat with music playing on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incredibly' looks like an anagram signal for 'small boat', but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Subatomic describes particles smaller than an atom, as tiny as things get.

clue.text: The last king of Scotland to back Prince Myshkin?

parts.note: Idi Amin styled himself the Last King of Scotland, the title of a novel and film about him

indicators.note: back means the little word to is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether the last Scottish monarch supported a Russian prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Myshkin is the title character of a Dostoevsky novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel The Idiot is named for its naive hero, Prince Myshkin.

clue.text: A Marxist piece in this Art Review

indicators.note: a piece in means a run of letters sitting inside the next words

parts.note: found running across the words

explanation.surface: An article by a Marxist appears in this arts magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre, the existentialist philosopher, embraced Marxism and called it the philosophy of his time.

clue.text: One who's not tried PG Wodehouse for a while

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone held without being brought to trial
second meaning: the author was held by the Germans in 1940-41

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not tried' looks like untested or unattempted, but it means never put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined, often in wartime, without any trial, as Wodehouse was in a German camp.
